# LegatorOCR 0.2.0-pre.61

- **Collections, limits closed:** `collection reindex` (and "Index text" / "Index all" in the window) indexes the text layer of PDFs that already have one, without reprocessing; `collection set` and `collection remove` change or drop items from the command line; double-click on a search result opens the PDF at that page when the default PDF viewer is a known one (otherwise it opens normally and the page is shown in the status line; macOS does not pass the page); the window uses the Tesseract path set in the main window; item-name guessing is smarter (`revista_sinteza_1985_03_12` → number 12, a day only when it is a real day of the month).
- **Faster index for large collections:** the index is one JSON line per item plus a deletable word cache; on a synthetic collection of 5000 items × 20 pages, opening took 62 ms with the cache (34 s before) and memory after opening 82 MB (481 MB before); a frequent word is found in 43 ms. A first open without the cache takes about 12 s. Old index files are still read and rewritten in the new format at the next save.
- Site and documentation brought up to date (thumbnails, upside-down pages, collections, hardware tutorial).

Known: the new buttons, the status line and open-at-page have not been looked at on screen; the viewer commands were never run against a real viewer; `reindex` does not do OCR.

- **Tuned on real photos** (25 phone photos of one book, 50 pages): the border-band rule of pre.59 changed nothing on 49 pages and wrongly widened the content box on one (strips of upholstery along the page edge were taken for text columns); a strip now counts as text only if it fills at least a quarter of its rectangle and has no row more than 4× the median row. The OCR rescue pass (lines Tesseract left out) recovered real text (+41 words on 50 pages) but once turned the page number "299" into "2.200" on its own line; a rescued line must now contain a word with at least 2 letters. On the table-of-contents pages the rescue pass did not help (3064 vs 3063 words). One book and one phone only.
